items.title: Output shaping: hide rate info by default; conditionally include via argument; hide pagination/meta when not applicable
items.body:
Summary
Adjust structuredContent meta fields across all tools so that:
- Rate limiter info is excluded by default and only included when an optional argument is provided.
- has_more and next_cursor are hidden when has_more == false.
- meta is hidden entirely when rate info is not requested AND has_more == false (no fields left to display).

Background
Current outputs always include meta with fields:
- next_cursor: Option<String>
- has_more: bool
- rate: Option<RateMeta>
This leads to null/false-y fields and rate details in responses by default. We want leaner defaults and an explicit opt-in for rate info.

Proposed behavior
- New optional per-call argument: _include_rate: boolean (default false)
  - Reserved input key at the top level of the tool arguments; unknown arguments are ignored by typed input deserializers, so this is backwards compatible.
- Default (no _include_rate or false):
  - If has_more == false: omit has_more and next_cursor, and omit the entire meta object if no other fields remain.
  - If has_more == true: include meta.has_more = true and meta.next_cursor; omit meta.rate.
- With _include_rate == true:
  - Always include meta.
  - If has_more == false: include only meta.rate (omit has_more/next_cursor).
  - If has_more == true: include meta.has_more, meta.next_cursor, and meta.rate.

Implementation approach (minimal change)
- Do not modify input structs or output types in this pass.
- In server handlers, after serializing the typed Output to serde_json::Value and before wrapping, prune meta fields based on _include_rate and has_more.
  - Add a helper, e.g., fn prune_meta(structured: &mut Value, include_rate: bool), that:
    - Locates structured["meta"].
    - If has_more == false (or missing/false): remove next_cursor and has_more.
    - If include_rate == false: remove rate.
    - If meta becomes empty after removals: remove structured["meta"].
- Read the optional _include_rate flag from the raw arguments Value (top-level key). Example:
  let include_rate = params.get("_include_rate").and_then(|v| v.as_bool()).unwrap_or(false);
- Apply the helper uniformly in all handle_* routes before calling mcp_wrap.

Notes and edge cases
- GraphQL: Rate meta is present only when the query includes rateLimit { remaining used resetAt }. Many queries already do; some do not. In those cases, meta.rate will remain None even when requested. This is acceptable for phase 1.
- REST: Endpoints using http::rest_* helpers have rate headers extracted; endpoints that bypass helpers (e.g., get_workflow_job_logs, rerun/cancel) won’t populate rate today. Also acceptable in phase 1.
- MCP envelope remains unchanged; only structuredContent is pruned.

Acceptance criteria
- Default behavior (no _include_rate provided):
  - When a non-paginated result is returned (has_more == false), structuredContent contains no meta field.
  - When a paginated result is returned (has_more == true), structuredContent.meta contains only:
    - has_more: true, next_cursor: <opaque string>. rate is omitted.
- With _include_rate = true:
  - For non-paginated results: structuredContent.meta contains only rate.
  - For paginated results: structuredContent.meta contains has_more, next_cursor, and rate.
- Apply consistently across all tools/handlers.
- Update README/docs to document the reserved _include_rate argument and the new default output shape.
- Add tests covering:
  - has_more=false with and without _include_rate
  - has_more=true with and without _include_rate
  - A GraphQL tool that includes rateLimit and a REST tool using rest helpers.

Out of scope (follow-up potential)
- Adding rateLimit selection to GraphQL queries that currently omit it.
- Plumbing rate info into endpoints that bypass REST helpers.

References
- Types: src/types.rs (RateMeta), src/tools.rs (Meta for tools)
- HTTP: src/http/mod.rs (extract_rate_from_rest, graphql_post)
- Server: src/server.rs (all handle_* routes), src/mcp.rs (mcp_wrap)

items.title: Replace live E2E with cargo integration tests; keep minimal Inspector smoke (tools/list + get_issue)
items.body:
Summary
- Remove existing live E2E tests and scripts.
- Implement comprehensive integration tests for each MCP tool using cargo test with HTTP/GraphQL mocking (httpmock), no real network by default.
- Keep a minimal E2E/smoke step using @modelcontextprotocol/inspector-cli to verify:
  1) tools/list returns descriptors and includes GitHub tools
  2) tools/call get_issue works against a known public test repo when GITHUB_TOKEN is available (skip gracefully on forks or missing token).

Background
The repository currently includes:
- docs/e2e and scripts/e2e_live.sh which drive broad live coverage via Inspector
- CI jobs e2e, e2e-live, e2e-live-mutations
- A solid suite of mocked integration tests under tests/ already covering many tools

Requested changes
1) Remove live E2E coverage
   - Delete docs/e2e/* and scripts/e2e_live.sh
   - Remove CI jobs e2e-live and e2e-live-mutations from .github/workflows/ci.yml
   - Update docs/testing.md to reflect the new strategy (mocked integration tests + minimal smoke)

2) Expand cargo integration tests to cover each tool
   - For each tool defined in src/tools.rs, add/ensure at least one integration test under tests/ that:
     - Calls the tool via the MCP envelope (stdin/stdout) using assert_cmd
     - Mocks the corresponding REST/GraphQL endpoint(s) with httpmock
     - Asserts on the structuredContent schema (presence of key fields, meta handling, and error shaping where relevant)
   - Keep tests read-only and self-contained. No external network calls.
   - Maintain existing grouping by domain (issues, PRs, actions, search, repos, etc.). Add missing tests for:
     - list_pr_files (unified + light), pr_summary, get_pr_diff/patch headers already exist – verify coverage sufficiency
     - commits/tags/branches/releases/get_release (light REST)
     - list_starred_repositories (REST)
     - search_issues/search_pull_requests/search_repositories
     - update_issue, update_pull_request (GraphQL/REST as implemented)
     - merge_pr and fork_repository (REST) – mocked 200/202 paths and common errors
     - list_repo_secrets_light, list_repo_variables_light, list_environments_light, list_environment_variables_light
   - Preserve gating behavior tests (e.g., ping enabled/disabled) and meta/rate opt-in behavior.

3) Keep minimal Inspector smoke in CI
   - Retain the existing e2e job but restrict it to:
     - Inspector tools/list (already present)
     - Inspector tools/call get_issue using E2E_OWNER/E2E_REPO/E2E_ISSUE_NUM fixtures. Use the default HautechAI/github-mcp-test-repo and issue 10, skip on forks or when no token.
   - Keep the stdio LF-only smoke.

Acceptance criteria
- CI workflow:
  - e2e-live and e2e-live-mutations jobs removed
  - e2e job runs Inspector tools/list and tools/call get_issue (skips gracefully if unauthenticated)
  - All cargo tests pass across OS matrix (linux, macOS, windows)
- Tests:
  - Each tool in src/tools.rs has at least one integration test
  - No tests depend on real network by default; httpmock used consistently
  - Meta handling verified: pagination next_cursor/has_more, and rate included only when explicitly requested
  - Ping gating behavior covered
- Docs:
  - docs/testing.md updated
  - docs/e2e removed

Notes
- If any tool is deprecated or gated, document and either exclude or add an ignored test with rationale.
- If write-path tools require special shapes, cover happy-path and a representative error with mocked responses.

items.body:
The information you provide here will be included in the Open Liberty beta blog post ([example](https://openliberty.io/blog/2020/08/05/jakarta-grpc-beta-20009.html)), which will be published on [openliberty.io/blog/](https://www.openliberty.io/blog/), and potentially elsewhere, to promote this beta feature/function of Open Liberty. For this post to be included in the beta issue please make sure that this is completed by the end of Friday following the GM (Tuesday). The beta and release blogs are created using automation and rely on you following the template's structure. **DO NOT REMOVE/ALTER THE `<GHA>` TAGS THROUGHOUT THIS TEMPLATE.**
   
    <GHA-BLOG-SUMMARY>


The [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) has emerged as the standard for AI applications to access real-time information from external sources. The Liberty MCP Server feature `mcpServer-1.0` allows developers to expose business logic or data from their applications, allowing it to be integrated into agentic AI workflows.

This beta release of Liberty includes important updates to the `mcpServer-1.0` feature, including asynchronous tool support, stateless mode support and a few bug fixes.

### Prerequisites
To use the `mcpServer-1.0` feature, it is required to have `Java 17` installed on your system.

## Implement Role-based access control for MCP tools  #33118 

Allow role requirements to be assigned to tools by using the RolesAllowed, PermitAll and DenyAll annotations on a tool method or on the class that declares a tool method.
        Refer to the annotation Javadoc and the [Jakarta Annotations spec](https://jakarta.ee/specifications/annotations/3.0/annotations-spec-3.0) (3.1 and 3.11-3.14) for how these annotations should be interpreted
    Only include tools that the user has access to when they request the list of tools
    Validate that the user has the required role when they execute a tool

## MCP: Add RequestId special argument type #33370

Add [the RequestId interface](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkus-mcp-server/blob/main/core/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkiverse/mcp/server/RequestId.java) and allow tools to retrieve it as a parameter.

We already have a similar object, so we can update it to match the Quarkus RequestId and move it to the API project.

Here is an example of what that would look like for a tool that calls an asynchronous Jakarta REST client:
```java
some example java code!
}
```
    
## MCP: Add Meta special argument type #33368

Add the [Meta](https://github.com/quarkiverse/quarkus-mcp-server/blob/main/core/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkiverse/mcp/server/Meta.java) interface to provide access to [the _meta data](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/index#meta) in the request.

Tools can add a Meta parameter to get access to this data.

------

## Allowing annotations in MCP Content objects

As specified in the [MCP specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/resources#annotations) we now allow MCP annotations to be added to Content objects returned from Tool methods. Note that these aren't Java annotations, rather they're extra fields that provide hints to clients on how to use and display the content. Included in the annotation is:

- `audience` field - the enum `Role` type indicating the intended audience for the content,
- `lastModified` field - a string value of the ISO 8601 formatted timestamp indicating when the content object was last modified
- `priority` field - a double value from `0.0` to `1.0` indicating the importance of the content object.

This can be added to tools as represented below.

```java
@Tool
public TextContent toolName(@ToolArg(name = "input") String input) {
    Content.Annotations annotations = new Content.Annotations(Role.USER,
                                                              Instant.now().toString(),
                                                              1.0);
    return new TextContent("My Generated Text", null, annotations);
}
```

Result:

```json
{
    "id": 1,
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "result": {
        "content": [
            {
                "annotations": {
                    "audience": "user",
                    "lastModified": "2025-12-11T12:31:04",
                    "priority": 1.0
                },
                "text": "My Generated Text",
                "type": "text"
            }
        ],
        "isError": false
    }
}
```

 
    </GHA-BLOG-SUMMARY>

## What happens next?
- Add the label to the blog issue for the beta you're targeting (e.g. `target:YY00X-beta`).
- Make sure this blog post is linked back to the Epic for this feature/function.
- Your paragraph will be included in the beta blog post. It might be edited for style and consistency.
- You will be asked to review a draft before publication.
    - Once you've approved the code review, close this issue. 
- If you would _also_ like to write a standalone blog post about your update (highly recommended), raise an issue on the [Open Liberty blogs repo](https://github.com/OpenLiberty/blogs/issues/new/choose). State in the issue that the blog post relates to a specific release so that we can ensure it is published on an appropriate date (it won't be the same day as the beta blog post).

items.title: `content` field in tool results is not forwarded to the model when widget is rendered
items.body:
## Summary

When a tool returns both `content` and `structuredContent` with a widget (`openai/outputTemplate`), the `content` field is not forwarded to the model. Only `structuredContent` is passed (as a raw JSON code block), causing the model to miss any info included in `content`. 

## Expected Behavior

Per the [MCP server documentation](https://developers.openai.com/apps-sdk/build/mcp-server):

> **`content`** – optional narration (Markdown or plaintext) for the model's response.

> The widget reads those payloads through `window.openai.toolOutput` and `window.openai.toolResponseMetadata`, while **the model only sees `structuredContent`/`content`**.

The model should receive both `structuredContent` and `content`, allowing developers to provide a short narration text (e.g., "Found 14 products") that guides the model's response.

## Actual Behavior

When a widget renders:
1. `structuredContent` is passed to the model as a `content_type: "code"` block with `language: "json"`
2. `content` is **not present** in the model's context
3. `_meta` is correctly forwarded to `tool_response_metadata`
4. A hidden system message is added: "The tool included embedded UI which has been displayed to the user"

The model then sees the full raw JSON from `structuredContent` and attempts to summarize it, echoing data (titles, prices, URLs, descriptions) that is already displayed in the widget UI.

## Reproduction

**MCP Server returns:**
return {
  content: [{ type: "text", text: "Found 14 products for \"jackets\"." }],
  structuredContent: { products: [...], searches: [...], brand: {...} },
  _meta: { apiBaseUrl: "...", subject: null },
};**Verified via MCP Inspector:**
- "Unstructured Content" shows: `"Found 14 products for "jackets"."`
- This confirms the server IS sending `content`

**Captured ChatGPT SSE stream (`/backend-api/f/conversation`):**
- Tool response message has `content.content_type: "code"` with `content.text` containing only `structuredContent` fields
- No trace of the `content` array text
- `_meta` appears in `metadata.chatgpt_sdk.tool_response_metadata` (proving MCP response is received)

## Impact

- Model loses the `content` field, which can have important information

## Environment

- `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`: 1.12.1
- Transport: `StreamableHTTPServerTransport`
- Tool has `openai/outputTemplate` set (widget renders)

## Questions

1. Is this intentional behavior when a widget is rendered?
2. If so, the documentation should clarify that `content` is ignored when `openai/outputTemplate` is set
3. If not, can this be fixed so `content` reaches the model alongside `structuredContent`?

items.title: Composite Tools: Support references to structured tool responses
[Bug] MCP Server Tool Response: structuredContent Displayed While content Array Ignored
items.body:
**Bug Description**
When an MCP server returns a tool response containing both `content` (array of text/data) and `structuredContent` (metadata), Claude Code only displays `structuredContent` and ignores `content`.

**Environment Info**
- Platform: darwin
- Terminal: tmux
- Version: 2.0.67
- Feedback ID: 6f82e95d-a1ab-409a-a310-e12b0b9f9a0b

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure `glab mcp serve` as an MCP server (stdio transport)
2. Call any glab tool, e.g., `glab_mr_list`
3. Observe that only `structuredContent` is displayed

## Expected Behavior
Display the `content` field (array of text items containing actual data like the MR list)

## Actual Behavior
Only shows `structuredContent` metadata:
```json
{"pagination":{"actual_end":1006,"actual_size":1006,"actual_start":0,"limit":50000,"offset":0,"total_size":1006,"truncated":false}}
```

## Evidence
MCP server logs (captured via wrapper script) show both fields are sent correctly by the server:

**Request:**
```json
{"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"glab_mr_list","arguments":{}},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2}
```

**Response (from glab mcp serve):**
```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "result": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Showing 8 open merge requests on synology/OrangeDrive. (Page 1)\n\n!1359\tsynology/OrangeDrive!1359\tfeat: support complex share paths...\n..."
      }
    ],
    "structuredContent": {
      "pagination": {
        "actual_end": 1006,
        "actual_size": 1006,
        "actual_start": 0,
        "limit": 50000,
        "offset": 0,
        "total_size": 1006,
        "truncated": false
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**What Claude Code displays to the user:**
Only the `structuredContent` portion - the actual MR list in `content` is completely ignored.

## Analysis
According to the MCP specification, `CallToolResult` supports both:
- `content`: Primary response data (array of content items like text, images)
- `structuredContent`: Optional structured metadata

The MCP SDK schema (found in the binary) correctly defines both fields:
```
mF=CY.extend({content:b.array(w9B).default([]),structuredContent:b.object({}).passthrough().optional(),isError:b.optional(b.boolean())})
```

The issue appears to be in the response rendering/display logic that extracts data from MCP tool results - it seems to prioritize or exclusively use `structuredContent` when present, ignoring `content`.

## Notes
- Issue likely introduced in v2.0.21 when `structuredContent` support was added (per CHANGELOG.md)
- Workaround: Use CLI commands directly via Bash tool instead of MCP tools
- The glab MCP server is working correctly - this is a Claude Code client-side parsing issue

## Wrapper Script Used for Logging
```bash
#!/bin/bash
LOG_FILE="${GLAB_MCP_LOG:-/tmp/glab-mcp-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log}"
exec 3>&1
log_with_timestamp() {
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1: $line" >> "$LOG_FILE"
    done
}
echo "=== glab mcp serve started at $(date) ===" >> "$LOG_FILE"
tee >(log_with_timestamp "IN" >&2 2>/dev/null) | \
    glab mcp serve 2>> "$LOG_FILE" | \
    tee >(log_with_timestamp "OUT" >&2 2>/dev/null)
```

items.title: Virtual MCP Server Not Preserving `_meta` Field in Responses

labels.name: go
labels.description: Pull requests that update go code

items.body:
## Summary

The Virtual MCP Server (vMCP) is not preserving the `_meta` field from backend MCP server responses when forwarding them to clients. According to the MCP specification, `_meta` is a reserved field that can appear in both requests and responses for protocol-level metadata, but our current implementation only extracts `_meta` from requests and discards it from responses.

## Problem Description

The Model Context Protocol specification defines `_meta` as a universal metadata field that can appear in:
- Request params (`JSONRPCRequest.params._meta`)
- Response results (all `Result` types inherit `_meta?: { [key: string]: unknown }`)
- Notifications (`JSONRPCNotification.params._meta`)
- Content blocks (`TextContent._meta`, `ImageContent._meta`, etc.)
- Entity definitions (`Tool._meta`, `Resource._meta`, `Prompt._meta`, etc.)

**Current Behavior:**
- ✅ vMCP correctly extracts `_meta` from incoming request params (`pkg/mcp/parser.go:224-230`)
- ✅ vMCP makes `_meta` available via context (`mcp.GetMCPMeta(ctx)`)
- ❌ vMCP **discards** `_meta` from backend responses when converting them to simplified maps
- ❌ vMCP **cannot restore** `_meta` when constructing response objects for clients

**Expected Behavior:**
vMCP should preserve `_meta` fields from backend responses and forward them to clients, enabling:
- Progress token propagation for long-running operations
- Distributed tracing through the full request/response cycle
- Custom metadata from backends reaching clients
- Full MCP specification compliance

## Root Cause Analysis

### Architecture Flow

```
Client Request (with _meta)
    ↓
vMCP Server (preserves request _meta ✅)
    ↓
Backend MCP Server
    ↓
Backend Response (with _meta)
    ↓
vMCP Client Conversion ❌ LOSES _meta HERE
    ↓
vMCP Server Response (without _meta)
    ↓
Client receives incomplete response ❌
```

### Code Analysis

#### 1. Backend Response Structure (Correct)

Backends return full MCP response objects with `_meta`:

```go
// From mark3labs/mcp-go SDK
type CallToolResult struct {
    Content           []Content            // Response content
    IsError           bool                 // Error flag
    StructuredContent map[string]any       // Optional structured output
    _meta             map[string]unknown   // ✅ Metadata present
}
```

**Reference:** [MCP Spec - CallToolResult schema](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/schema#calltoolresult)

#### 2. Client Conversion Layer (Bug Location)

File: `pkg/vmcp/client/client.go:391-476`

```go
func (h *httpBackendClient) CallTool(
    ctx context.Context,
    target *vmcp.BackendTarget,
    toolName string,
    arguments map[string]any,
) (map[string]any, error) {
    // ...

    result, err := c.CallTool(ctx, mcp.CallToolRequest{
        Params: mcp.CallToolParams{
            Name:      backendToolName,
            Arguments: arguments,
        },
    })
    if err != nil {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("...")
    }

    // ❌ BUG: Convert result contents to simplified map, discarding _meta
    resultMap := make(map[string]any)
    if len(result.Content) > 0 {
        for i, content := range result.Content {
            if textContent, ok := mcp.AsTextContent(content); ok {
                resultMap["text"] = textContent.Text
            } else if imageContent, ok := mcp.AsImageContent(content); ok {
                resultMap["image"] = imageContent.Data
            }
            // _meta from result is never copied to resultMap
        }
    }

    return resultMap, nil  // ← Returns without _meta
}
```

**Problem:** The conversion from `mcp.CallToolResult` to `map[string]any` extracts only content fields and discards the `_meta` field entirely.

#### 3. Interface Definition (Design Issue)

File: `pkg/vmcp/types.go:247-263`

```go
type BackendClient interface {
    // CallTool invokes a tool on the backend MCP server.
    // Returns the tool output or an error.
    CallTool(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget, toolName string, arguments map[string]any) (map[string]any, error)

    // ReadResource retrieves a resource from the backend MCP server.
    // Returns the resource content or an error.
    ReadResource(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget, uri string) ([]byte, error)

    // GetPrompt retrieves a prompt from the backend MCP server.
    // Returns the rendered prompt text or an error.
    GetPrompt(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget, name string, arguments map[string]any) (string, error)
}
```

**Problem:** The interface returns simplified types (`map[string]any`, `[]byte`, `string`) instead of full MCP response structures that would include `_meta`.

#### 4. Handler Factory (Cannot Fix Without Upstream Data)

File: `pkg/vmcp/server/adapter/handler_factory.go:71-113`

```go
func (f *DefaultHandlerFactory) CreateToolHandler(
    toolName string,
) func(context.Context, mcp.CallToolRequest) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error) {
    return func(ctx context.Context, request mcp.CallToolRequest) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error) {
        // ...

        // Call backend - receives map without _meta
        result, err := f.backendClient.CallTool(ctx, target, toolName, args)
        if err != nil {
            return mcp.NewToolResultError(err.Error()), nil
        }

        // ❌ Cannot restore _meta here - it was already lost upstream
        return mcp.NewToolResultStructuredOnly(result), nil
    }
}
```

**Problem:** By the time we construct the response for the client, `_meta` has already been discarded in the conversion layer.

## Impact Assessment

### Affected Operations

All MCP operations that return structured results are affected:

1. **Tool Calls** (`tools/call`)
   - Missing `_meta` in `CallToolResult`
   - Cannot propagate progress tokens, trace IDs, or custom metadata

2. **Resource Reads** (`resources/read`)
   - Missing `_meta` in `ReadResourceResult`
   - Cannot propagate resource-specific metadata

3. **Prompt Gets** (`prompts/get`)
   - Missing `_meta` in `GetPromptResult`
   - Cannot propagate prompt-related metadata

4. **List Operations** (`tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`)
   - Missing `_meta` in `ListToolsResult`, `ListResourcesResult`, `ListPromptsResult`
   - Cannot propagate pagination metadata, cache hints, etc.

5. **Capability Discovery** (`initialize`)
   - Missing `_meta` in `InitializeResult`
   - Cannot propagate server-specific initialization metadata

### MCP Specification Compliance

According to the [MCP specification (2025-06-18)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/index):

> The `_meta` property/parameter is reserved by MCP to allow clients and servers to attach additional metadata to their interactions.

All `Result` types in the spec inherit the base `Result` interface:

```typescript
interface Result {
  _meta?: { [key: string]: unknown };
  [key: string]: unknown;
}
```

**vMCP is currently non-compliant** with this aspect of the specification.

### Use Cases Broken

1. **Progress Reporting**
   - Backends cannot report progress via `progressToken` in responses
   - Clients cannot track long-running operations

2. **Distributed Tracing**
   - Trace context (e.g., `traceparent`) is lost in responses
   - End-to-end tracing through vMCP is incomplete

3. **Custom Backend Metadata**
   - Backend-specific metadata (caching hints, rate limits, etc.) is discarded
   - Clients cannot make informed decisions based on backend state

4. **MCP Tasks (November 2025 Spec)**
   - Task-related metadata (`io.modelcontextprotocol/related-task`) must be preserved
   - See: [Related Task Metadata](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/utilities/tasks)
   - Current implementation cannot support task association metadata in responses

## Affected Code Locations

### Core Issue
- `pkg/vmcp/client/client.go:391-476` - `CallTool` conversion loses `_meta`
- `pkg/vmcp/client/client.go:479-534` - `ReadResource` conversion loses `_meta`
- `pkg/vmcp/client/client.go:535-596` - `GetPrompt` conversion loses `_meta`

### Interface Definition
- `pkg/vmcp/types.go:247-263` - `BackendClient` interface returns simplified types

### Handler Layer
- `pkg/vmcp/server/adapter/handler_factory.go:71-113` - `CreateToolHandler`
- `pkg/vmcp/server/adapter/handler_factory.go:115-169` - `CreateResourceHandler`
- `pkg/vmcp/server/adapter/handler_factory.go:171-244` - `CreatePromptHandler`

### Request Parsing (Working Correctly)
- `pkg/mcp/parser.go:224-230` - Request `_meta` extraction ✅
- `pkg/mcp/parser.go:478-485` - `GetMCPMeta` context helper ✅

## Proposed Solution

### Option 1: Rich Response Types (Recommended)

Change `BackendClient` interface to return full MCP response structures:

```go
type BackendClient interface {
    // Returns full CallToolResult including _meta
    CallTool(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget, toolName string, arguments map[string]any) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error)

    // Returns full ReadResourceResult including _meta
    ReadResource(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget, uri string) (*mcp.ReadResourceResult, error)

    // Returns full GetPromptResult including _meta
    GetPrompt(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget, name string, arguments map[string]any) (*mcp.GetPromptResult, error)

    // ListCapabilities should also return full results with _meta
    ListCapabilities(ctx context.Context, target *BackendTarget) (*CapabilityList, error)
}
```

**Advantages:**
- Full MCP spec compliance
- Preserves all response metadata
- Type-safe - compiler enforces correct usage
- Easier to add support for future MCP features

**Disadvantages:**
- Requires updating all `BackendClient` implementations
- Breaking change to internal API

### Option 2: Metadata Wrapper

Add metadata wrapper around results:

```go
type ResponseWithMeta struct {
    Result map[string]any
    Meta   map[string]any  // Preserved _meta field
}

type BackendClient interface {
    CallTool(...) (*ResponseWithMeta, error)
    // ...
}
```

**Advantages:**
- Smaller change than Option 1
- Preserves existing result structure

**Disadvantages:**
- Not type-safe for different response types
- Still requires interface changes
- Less aligned with MCP specification types

### Option 3: Context-Based Metadata

Store response metadata in context:

```go
type responseMetaKey struct{}

func SetResponseMeta(ctx context.Context, meta map[string]any) context.Context {
    return context.WithValue(ctx, responseMetaKey{}, meta)
}

func GetResponseMeta(ctx context.Context) map[string]any {
    if meta, ok := ctx.Value(responseMetaKey{}).(map[string]any); ok {
        return meta
    }
    return nil
}
```

**Advantages:**
- No interface changes required
- Can be added incrementally

**Disadvantages:**
- Implicit - easy to forget to propagate
- Context pollution
- Not idiomatic for response data
- Difficult to track metadata flow

## Recommendation

**Implement Option 1 (Rich Response Types)** for these reasons:

1. **Spec Alignment**: Directly aligns with MCP specification types
2. **Type Safety**: Compiler enforces correct metadata handling
3. **Future-Proof**: Easy to add new MCP features (e.g., structured tool outputs)
4. **Clarity**: Explicit response structure, no hidden context magic
5. **Testability**: Easy to verify metadata preservation in tests

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Interface Update
1. Update `BackendClient` interface to return full MCP response types
2. Update `httpBackendClient` implementation to preserve `_meta`
3. Update mock implementations for tests

### Phase 2: Conversion Layer
1. Remove simplified conversion logic in `pkg/vmcp/client/client.go`
2. Return full `mcp.CallToolResult`, `mcp.ReadResourceResult`, etc.
3. Preserve `_meta` field from backend responses

### Phase 3: Handler Adaptation
1. Update handler factory to use full response types
2. Forward `_meta` from backend responses to client responses
3. Merge/combine `_meta` fields when aggregating multiple backends (if needed)

### Phase 4: Testing
1. Add tests for `_meta` preservation in responses
2. Add integration tests with real MCP servers
3. Test distributed tracing flow
4. Test progress token propagation

### Phase 5: Documentation
1. Update architecture documentation
2. Document `_meta` handling in vMCP
3. Add examples for custom metadata

## Testing Considerations

### Unit Tests

```go
func TestCallTool_PreservesMetaInResponse(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange: Backend returns response with _meta
    expectedMeta := map[string]any{
        "progressToken": "abc123",
        "traceparent": "00-trace-id-01",
        "custom.backend/hint": "cache-hit",
    }

    // Act: Call tool through vMCP
    result, err := client.CallTool(ctx, target, "test_tool", args)

    // Assert: _meta is preserved
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Equal(t, expectedMeta, result._meta)
}
```

### Integration Tests

```go
func TestVMCP_EndToEndMetaPropagation(t *testing.T) {
    // Test full flow: Client → vMCP → Backend → vMCP → Client
    // Verify _meta propagates through entire chain
}
```

### Compatibility Tests

```go
func TestVMCP_BackwardCompatibility(t *testing.T) {
    // Verify vMCP handles backends that don't return _meta
    // (should not break, just omit _meta in response)
}
```

## References

- [MCP Specification (2025-06-18) - _meta field](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/index#_meta)
- [MCP Schema - Result types](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/schema#result)
- [MCP Tasks - Related Task Metadata](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/utilities/tasks)
- [W3C Trace Context](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/) - Common use case for _meta

## Additional Context

### Current Request _meta Handling (For Comparison)

Request `_meta` is correctly handled:

```go
// pkg/mcp/parser.go:224-230
var meta map[string]interface{}
if metaRaw, ok := paramsMap["_meta"]; ok {
    if metaMap, ok := metaRaw.(map[string]interface{}); ok {
        meta = metaMap  // ✅ Preserved in context
    }
}
```

We should apply the same preservation approach to response `_meta`.

### MCP Specification Quote

From the spec:

> Certain key names are reserved by MCP for protocol-level metadata... implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at these keys.

This means vMCP should act as a transparent proxy for `_meta` fields, preserving them without interpretation or modification (except for aggregation scenarios where merging may be needed).

items.title: on_call_tool middleware return value discarded — wire response uses inner result

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working. Reports of errors, unexpected behavior, or broken functionality.

labels.name: server
labels.description: Related to FastMCP server implementation or server-side functionality.

items.body:
### Description

`on_call_tool` middleware return value is silently discarded. The wire response always contains the result from `call_next()`, not the modified/replaced `ToolResult` returned by middleware.

Related to #1252 (which was about returning the wrong type — `CallToolResult` vs `ToolResult`). This issue is different: we return the correct `ToolResult` type, but the value is still discarded.

### MRE

```python
from fastmcp import FastMCP
from fastmcp.server.middleware.middleware import Middleware
from fastmcp.tools.tool import ToolResult
from mcp.types import TextContent
import json

mcp = FastMCP("test")

class InjectMiddleware(Middleware):
    async def on_call_tool(self, context, call_next):
        result = await call_next(context)
        if result.content and hasattr(result.content[0], "text"):
            data = json.loads(result.content[0].text)
            data["injected"] = True
            return ToolResult(content=[TextContent(type="text", text=json.dumps(data))])
        return result

mcp.add_middleware(InjectMiddleware())

@mcp.tool
async def hello() -> dict:
    return {"ok": True, "message": "hello"}
```

**Expected**: Response includes `"injected": true`
**Actual**: Response only contains `{"ok": true, "message": "hello"}`

In-place mutation (`result.content[0].text = ...`) also doesn't survive to wire. Confirmed via file-based logging that the middleware runs and the mutation/replacement happens in-memory.

### Environment

- fastmcp 3.1.1, Python 3.14, stdio transport

items.title: [Bug]: MCP tool adapter drops structuredContent and only forwards content text
items.body:
## Summary

Hermes's MCP tool adapter currently drops `structuredContent` from `CallToolResult` and only forwards concatenated `content[*].text` back into the agent/tool result.

That breaks MCP tools that return a minimal human text like `OK` in `content`, while putting the actual machine-usable payload in `structuredContent`.

## Repro

A minimal MCP tool result like this is enough to trigger it:

```json
{
  "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "OK"}],
  "structuredContent": {
    "result": {
      "value": "actual-secret-or-username",
      "revealed": true
    }
  },
  "isError": false
}
```

With current Hermes behavior, the model/tool loop only sees `OK` and loses the actual payload.

## Actual behavior

Hermes only joins the text blocks from `result.content` and returns:

```json
{"result": "OK"}
```

## Expected behavior

At minimum Hermes should preserve `structuredContent` instead of discarding it.

Examples of acceptable fixes:

- include both `content` and `structuredContent` in the serialized tool result returned to the agent
- or, if Hermes wants a text-only fallback, serialize `structuredContent` into the returned payload in addition to the plain text

## Why this matters

This breaks otherwise valid MCP servers that rely on `structuredContent` for the real output, especially keychain/credential-style tools where the human text is intentionally terse.

## Code pointers

Hermes currently drops `structuredContent` here:

- [`tools/mcp_tool.py#L1238-L1256`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/tools/mcp_tool.py#L1238-L1256)

The adapter only reads `result.content[*].text` and never forwards `result.structuredContent`.

## Notes

This seems distinct from transport/session issues. In our case the MCP call succeeded, but Hermes flattened the successful result into text-only output and lost the structured payload.

items.title: expect_error steps can't validate controller error response fields
items.body:
## Summary

Storyboard steps with `expect_error: true` that call `comply_test_controller` cannot validate error response fields (`success`, `error`, `error_detail`). The validations resolve `undefined` for all paths.

## Root cause

When the controller returns `isError: true` in the MCP response, the MCP client throws an exception with the text content (e.g., `"Controller error: UNKNOWN_SCENARIO"`). The storyboard runner catches this in `runStep` and sets `stepResult.error` to the message string.

The `extractErrorData` function in `runner.ts` tries to parse this error message, but it only handles two patterns:
1. JSON with `adcp_error` structure
2. `"code": "ERROR_CODE"` pattern

The controller error message (`"Controller error: UNKNOWN_SCENARIO"`) doesn't match either. A third pattern was added for controller errors but it's not being reached because `taskResult` is not null/undefined in the step execution path — `executeStoryboardTask` returns a result with `success: false` before the throw is caught.

The deeper issue is that `structuredContent` from MCP error responses (which contains the full `{ success: false, error: "UNKNOWN_SCENARIO" }` payload) is discarded when `callMCPTool` throws. The error data should be extracted from `structuredContent` before falling back to text parsing.

## Affected steps

`deterministic_testing` storyboard:
- `unknown_scenario` — expects `{ success: false, error: "UNKNOWN_SCENARIO" }`
- `missing_params` — expects `{ success: false, error: "INVALID_PARAMS" }`  
- `not_found_entity` — expects `{ success: false, error: "NOT_FOUND" }`

## Proposed fix

Two options:

**Option A**: Preserve `structuredContent` from MCP error responses. When `callMCPTool` encounters `isError: true`, instead of throwing, return a `TaskResult` with `success: false` and `data` populated from `structuredContent`. This would make error data available to validations without text parsing.

**Option B**: Use `callMCPToolRaw` (which already exists and doesn't throw on `isError`) for `comply_test_controller` calls in the storyboard task map. This preserves the full response including structured data.

items.title: [Bug]:  MCP client discards text content when structuredContent is present

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

When an MCP server returns both `content` (text) and `structuredContent` (metadata JSON), the Hermes MCP client only keeps `structuredContent` and silently discards `content`. This means the AI agent receives only metadata (e.g. fileName, filePath) but not the actual file content or text output from the MCP server.

The MCP spec defines both fields for different purposes:
- `content` — human/AI-readable text or images
- `structuredContent` — machine-readable JSON metadata

They should be combined, not treated as mutually exclusive alternatives.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure any MCP server that returns both `content` and `structuredContent` (e.g. Desktop Commander MCP v0.2.38 with `read_file`)
2. Run `hermes chat`
3. Call the MCP tool: "Read the file /etc/os-release"
4. Observe that the response contains only `{fileName, filePath, fileType}` — no actual file content

### Expected Behavior

The AI agent should receive both the file content (from `content` field) AND the metadata (from `structuredContent` field). The response should contain the actual text data the agent needs to answer the user's question.

### Actual Behavior

The agent only receives structured metadata like `{"fileName": "os-release", "filePath": "/etc/os-release", "fileType": "text"}`. The actual file content is silently dropped. The agent cannot answer questions about the file because it never sees the data.

### Affected Component

Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.), CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Operating System

Fedora (SELinux enforcing)

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

 latest

### Relevant Logs / Traceback

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The bug is in `tools/mcp_tool.py` around line 1258-1262 in the MCP tool handler function:

```python
# Prefer structuredContent (machine-readable JSON) over plain text
structured = getattr(result, "structuredContent", None)
if structured is not None:
    return json.dumps({"result": structured})  # ← discards text_result
return json.dumps({"result": text_result})

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Replace lines 1258-1262 in `tools/mcp_tool.py`:

```python
# Before (buggy):
structured = getattr(result, "structuredContent", None)
if structured is not None:
    return json.dumps({"result": structured})
return json.dumps({"result": text_result})

# After (fixed):
structured = getattr(result, "structuredContent", None)
if structured is not None:
    if text_result:
        if isinstance(structured, dict):
            structured = {**structured, "content": text_result}
        else:
            structured = {"structured": structured, "content": text_result}
    return json.dumps({"result": structured})
return json.dumps({"result": text_result})
```

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

## 🧱 Target architecture

### 🥇 GOLD I — `trios-igla-race-pipeline`

```
crates/trios-igla-race-pipeline/
├── Cargo.toml                     # workspace member
├── README.md  · TASK.md  · AGENTS.md   # I5 mandatory
├── RING.md                        # GOLD ring spec
├── src/lib.rs                     # facade only (L-ARCH-001, ≤ 50 LoC, pub use only)
└── rings/
    ├── SR-00/  scarab-types         (extracted from neon.rs + status.rs; serde + uuid + chrono)
    ├── SR-01/  strategy-queue       (hive_automaton.rs + pull_queue.rs)
    ├── SR-02/  trainer-runner       (sampler + attn + gf16 + git dep `trios-trainer-igla`)
    ├── SR-03/  bpb-writer           (bpb.rs + ema.rs + neon.rs (write side) + migrations)
    ├── SR-04/  gardener             (asha + invariants + race + nca + rungs + lessons)

    └── BR-OUTPUT/                   (IglaRacePipeline assembler + integration tests)
```

**Dependency flow (R1 isolation):** `BR-OUTPUT → SR-05 → SR-04 → SR-03 → SR-02 → SR-01 → SR-00`. Strict monotone numbering; no sibling imports.

**E2E TTT O(1) loop sketch (BR-OUTPUT):**

```rust
impl IglaRacePipeline {
    pub async fn run_e2e_ttt_o1(&mut self) -> Result<VictoryReport, PipelineErr> {
        loop {
            let job = self.queue.claim_one().await?;            // O(1)
            for chunk in self.runner.stream_chunks(&job)? {     // O(1) per chunk
                let bpb = self.runner.step_one_chunk(chunk)?;   // O(1) — E2E TTT
                self.writer.write_one(&job, &bpb).await?;       // O(1)
                if self.gardener.should_prune(&job, &bpb).await? { break; }
            }
            if self.gardener.is_victory(&job).await? {           // INV-7 igla_found_criterion
                return Ok(self.gardener.victory_report(&job).await?);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### 🥇 GOLD II — `trios-algorithm-arena` (Variant A)

```

├── SR-ALG-01/  jepa                    (parameter-golf wishlist #3)
├── SR-ALG-02/  universal-transformer   (parameter-golf wishlist #6)

├── SR-ALG-06/  megakernels             (parameter-golf wishlist #7)
└── BR-OUTPUT/                          (AlgorithmArena assembler — `run_one(algo, seed) -> Bpb`)
```

Each SR holds **only metadata**:

```rust
pub struct AlgorithmSpec {
    pub entry_path: PathBuf,           // e.g. records/track_10min_16mb/2026-03-17_LoRA_TTT/train_gpt.py
    pub entry_hash: [u8; 32],          // SHA-256, verified before invocation
    pub env: Vec<(EnvVar, EnvValue)>,  // gated env vars per parameter-golf convention

}
```

The Python `train_gpt.py` itself stays inside `parameter-golf/records/<entry>/` — never inside `crates/`. SR-02 trainer-runner spawns it as a subprocess after `entry_hash` verification.

items.title: fix(adapter): hello_seller_adapter_proposal_mode create_media_buy fails schema validation against AdCP 3.0.7
items.body:
## Problem

After AdCP 3.0.7 (#1595) landed, the proposal-mode adapter gate test fails on the \`create_media_buy\` step:

\`\`\`
✗ create_media_buy — Create media buy from proposal
    Response matches create-media-buy-response.json schema
\`\`\`

This was previously masked: \`get_products_refine\` failed in 3.0.6 (literal \`balanced_reach_q2\` placeholder, no \`context_outputs\` chaining), which cascade-skipped \`create_media_buy\`. AdCP 3.0.7 fixed the chaining via [adcp#4088](https://github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp/pull/4088), so \`get_products_refine\` now passes — and \`create_media_buy\` actually runs against the upstream, where the response shape doesn't satisfy the 3.0.7 \`create-media-buy-response.json\` schema.

## What needs to happen

1. Boot \`examples/hello_seller_adapter_proposal_mode.ts\` locally, run \`adcp storyboard run\` against it, and capture the actual response payload from \`create_media_buy\`.
2. Compare against \`schemas/cache/3.0.7/bundled/.../create-media-buy-response.json\`.
3. Identify which field is missing/wrong in the adapter's wire-shape projection (likely a renamed/added required field in 3.0.7).
4. Fix \`examples/hello_seller_adapter_proposal_mode.ts\` to emit the correct shape.

## Workaround

Until this is fixed, the gate test allowlist masks \`create_media_buy\` (PR #1599).

## Refs

- adcp-client#1599 — adds \`create_media_buy\` to EXPECTED_FAILURES allowlist
- adcp-client#1594 — original adapter PR
- adcp-client#1595 — 3.0.7 bump that exposed this
- adcp#4088 — the 3.0.7 storyboard fix that uncovered the cascade

items.title: [docs] Deep-dive: claude-agent-sdk vs codex-sdk adapter comparison
items.body:
## 背景

anet 现在内置 3 个 runtime：
- `claude-agent-sdk` — Anthropic 官方 `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`
- `codex-sdk` — OpenAI 官方 `@openai/codex-sdk`
- `claude-code-cli` — spawn 本机 `claude` 二进制（不属于 SDK 范畴）

前两个 SDK 在 anet 里的接入语义、能力边界、session 处理、tool 注册、streaming、token 计费、错误处理等**没有专门系统化对比**。`docs-site/docs/guide/runtimes.md` 给的是 user-facing how-to，对"想自己接新 SDK"或"想理解 anet 怎么 wrap SDK"的 contributor 不够深。

## 目标

通信SDK马 出一份 SDK adapter 深度对比，结论落 docs。

## 调研维度（建议）

| 维度 | claude-agent-sdk | codex-sdk |
|---|---|---|
| package / 版本 | | |
| API entry（query / thread / etc.） | | |
| Session 语义（id 来源 / 持久化 / resume 接口） | | |
| Tool 注册（MCP / 内置） | | |
| Streaming（SSE / async iterator / Promise） | | |
| Token 计费 / 预算（`--max-budget` 谁实现） | | |
| 错误处理 + 重试 | | |
| 多 turn 行为 + history 限制 | | |
| ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL / 等价机制（路由到 MiniMax / DeepSeek / Codex provider） | | |
| settingSources / 项目隔离 | | |
| breaking change cadence + 历史 | | |
| anet wrapper 关键代码位置 | agent-node/src/cli.ts:546 区域 | agent-node/src/cli.ts:673 区域 |

## 交付物

- 新文件 `docs-site/docs/guide/sdk-deep-dive.md` + EN 镜像 `docs-site/docs/en/guide/sdk-deep-dive.md`
- 内容：对比表 + 各 SDK 接入注意事项 + anet wrapper 怎么收敛差异 + 想加新 runtime（gemini-cli / qwen-code 等）应该怎么照葫芦画瓢
- `.vitepress/config.ts` ZH+EN sidebar 加链接到新文件
- `docs-site/docs/guide/runtimes.md` 末尾加"想深入？→ SDK Deep-dive"指引

## 不要做

- 不改 cli.ts / agent-node 源码（纯文档 + 调研）
- 不发新 npm 版本
- 不动 hub / dashboard

## 流程

- 按 [#15 Phase 0 PR pipeline](https://github.com/sleep2agi/agent-network/pull/16) 走 worktree + PR
- worktree 路径：`~/anet-work/sdk-deep-dive/`
- 分支：`docs/sdk-deep-dive`
- PR description 用新 template，`Closes #` 这个 issue

## 验收

- 文档构建 `npm run build` 通过无 dead link
- ZH + EN 内容齐
- sidebar 能跳到新文档
- 对比表至少覆盖上方"调研维度"表里列的项

items.title: feat(sdk): OpenAI Responses API tool — second tool under ./openai subpath
items.body:
## Summary

Add `client.responses.create` (OpenAI Responses API) as a second MCP tool under the `./openai` subpath, alongside the existing `chat-completions` tool. Validates the provider-one, API-many registry pattern.

## Goals

- Expose a `responses` MCP tool that preserves reasoning content for o-series models (o1/o3/o4) via `structuredContent.reasoning`
- Reuse `createOpenAIClient`, `mapOpenAIError`, and the `ToolDescriptor` shape from `openai/chat.ts` — no new SDK dependency (`openai@^6` already exposes Responses)
- Register both `chat-completions` and `responses` tools on the same server via `registerOpenAIProvider`

## Constraints

- MCP tool input: `{ messages }` only — no caller-supplied `model` (server is the single source of truth per existing policy)
- Streaming: handle `response.output_text.delta`, `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta`, `response.completed`; ignore all other v1 event types
- Reasoning text surfaces as `structuredContent.reasoning` only — never concatenated into assistant content
- Usage normalized: `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` → `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`/`total_tokens`
- New optional env: `AI_RELAY_REASONING_EFFORT` (`'low' | 'medium' | 'high'`) — server-side only, not a per-call input field
- Cancellation: same AbortController + `maxRetries: 0` invariant as `chat.ts`
- v1 carve-outs: no `previous_response_id`, no built-in tools, no function calling, no image/audio input

**Related Files:**
- `packages/ai-relay/src/openai/index.ts:32` — `registerOpenAIProvider` to extend
- `packages/ai-relay/src/openai/chat.ts:147` — `mapOpenAIError` to reuse
- `packages/ai-relay/src/openai/chat.ts:250` — `ToolDescriptor` interface to implement
- `packages/ai-relay/src/openai/client.ts` — `createOpenAIClient` factory to reuse
- `packages/ai-relay/src/bin/registry.ts:48` — add `"responses"` key to openai tools map

> **Next:** Requires `/plan` to produce a full implementation plan.

<details><summary>Original Issue</summary>

## Goal

Add **OpenAI Responses API** (`client.responses.create`) as a second MCP tool under the existing `./openai` subpath. No new SDK dependency — `openai@^6` already exposes it.

Depends on #90 (ADR) and #91 (Anthropic + provider-aware refactor — establishes the multi-API-per-provider registry pattern).

## Why

- Chat Completions discards reasoning content for o-series models (o1/o3/o4). Responses preserves it via `response.reasoning_summary.*` stream events.
- OpenAI's recommended forward path is Responses for new integrations.
- Validates the **provider-one, API-many** pattern: same registry entry exposes both `chat-completions` and `responses` tools.

## Scope

### New code

- `packages/ai-relay/src/openai/responses.ts`:
  - `registerOpenAIResponses(server, config)` + `makeOpenAIResponsesHandler(config)` + `openAIResponsesTool` ToolDescriptor
  - Reuses `createOpenAIClient` factory (no client refactor needed)
- `packages/ai-relay/src/openai/index.ts`:
  - Re-export `registerOpenAIResponses` and `openAIResponsesTool`
  - Update `registerOpenAIProvider` to register both tools on the same server
- `packages/ai-relay/src/bin/registry.ts`:
  - Add `responses` to `tools` map under the `openai` entry

### MCP tool input schema

```ts
z.object({
  messages: z.array(z.object({
    role: z.enum(['system', 'user', 'assistant']),
    content: z.string(),
  })).min(1),
}).strict()
```

Same caller surface as Chat Completions (per #90 decision 3). Inside the handler, translate to Responses `input` format (array of `{ role, content: [{ type: 'input_text', text }] }`).

### Streaming

`client.responses.create({ stream: true, … })` emits ~30 event types. v1 handles:

- `response.output_text.delta` → accumulate `delta` string into the assistant text
- `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` → accumulate into a **separate** `reasoning` string surfaced via `structuredContent.reasoning` (NOT concatenated into the assistant content)
- `response.completed` → final usage (`usage.input_tokens`, `usage.output_tokens`)
- All other events ignored in v1 (function calls, file search, web search, image generation — those are v2 backlog items)

### Output schema

```ts
{
  content: [{ type: 'text', text: <accumulated output_text> }],
  structuredContent: {
    model: string,
    usage?: { prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens },
    finish_reason?: string,
    reasoning?: string,
  },
  isError: boolean
}
```

### Error mapping

Identical taxonomy to Chat Completions. Same `mapOpenAIError` helper can be reused.

### Cancellation

Same AbortController pattern as `openai/chat.ts:215-225`. Same streaming invariant: `maxRetries: 0`.

### v1 carve-outs (NOT in this issue)

- `previous_response_id` chaining — out of scope
- Built-in tools — v2 backlog
- Function/tool calling — v2 backlog
- Image / audio input — v2

## Env / config

New optional env: `AI_RELAY_REASONING_EFFORT` — `'low' | 'medium' | 'high'` for o-series. Server-side only.

## Tests

- `packages/ai-relay/tests/unit/openai-responses.test.ts`
- `packages/ai-relay/tests/unit/multi-registration.test.ts` — add coexistence case
- `tests/integration/route.test.ts` — extend `tools/list` assertion

## Docs

- `packages/ai-relay/README.md`
- `doc/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4 + §11
- `README.md`
- `doc/QA-MCP-INSPECTOR.md`

</details>

items.title: tools: return structured tool results with text fallback

labels.name: tool-use debacle
labels.description: Workstream for Stirrup tool-use reliability improvements

labels.name: tools
labels.description: Tool registry, tool schemas, and tool execution UX

items.body:
## Type

Feature request

## Motivation

Most Stirrup tool results are currently returned as one text string. That works for broad provider compatibility, but it makes tool outputs harder for models and downstream systems to parse reliably. Command results, search hits, and file excerpts are all better represented with stable fields such as path, line, text, stdout, stderr, and exit code.

Structured results should improve model reliability while preserving a text fallback for providers that only accept string tool results.

## Current state

- `types.ToolResult` has `Content string` and `IsError`.
- `run_command` concatenates stdout, stderr, and exit code into a string.
- `search_files` returns raw grep/find output.
- `read_file` returns raw file content.
- MCP `tools/call` handling preserves text content only and drops non-text content, structured content, resource links, output schemas, and annotations.

## Goals

1. Add a structured result representation alongside the existing text content.
2. Preserve text fallback for all providers.
3. Return structured command results, including `stdout`, `stderr`, `exit_code`, and timeout metadata.
4. Return structured search matches, including path, line, column if available, and match text.
5. Return structured file excerpts, including path, start line, end line, truncation state, and text lines.
6. Preserve richer MCP result content where supported.

## Non-goals

- Requiring all providers to accept non-string tool results immediately.
- Changing the executor API more than needed.
- Building a UI for structured results.

## Design considerations

- Keep `Content string` for backwards compatibility and provider fallback.
- Consider adding `Structured json.RawMessage` or a typed result envelope to `types.ToolResult`.
- Provider adapters should serialize structured results only when the provider supports the shape; otherwise they should send the text fallback.
- Trace output should include structured data when safe and scrubbed.
- MCP support should track the current MCP tool result spec, including `structuredContent`, resource links, embedded resources, and non-text content.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ToolResult` can carry structured data without breaking existing text-only flows.
- Built-in command/search/read results populate structured data and text fallback consistently.
- Provider adapters preserve compatibility with current string result behavior.
- MCP bridge preserves at least text plus structured content where available; unsupported content types are represented or explicitly marked rather than silently discarded.
- Tests cover provider serialization, built-in tool structured output, and MCP structured output handling.
- Docs describe the result envelope and provider fallback behavior.
- `go test ./harness/... ./types/...` passes.

## References

- `types/messages.go` — `ToolResult`
- `harness/internal/tool/builtins/shell.go`
- `harness/internal/tool/builtins/search.go`
- `harness/internal/tool/builtins/filesystem.go`
- `harness/internal/mcp/client.go` — MCP `tools/call` result handling
- MCP tools spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools

items.title: bug(socrata_query_dataset): SoQL 400 errors swallow upstream message and bypass soql_error contract

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Worked before, broken after a change

items.body:
### Server version

0.1.0

### mcp-ts-core version

^0.9.7

### Runtime

Bun

### Transport

HTTP

### Description

When Socrata returns HTTP 400 for an invalid SoQL query, the error surfaces as a generic "Socrata returned HTTP 400 Bad Request." with no upstream message and no `soql_error` reason. The declared `soql_error` error contract entry (with its recovery hint) is never triggered because `fetchJson` only maps a narrow set of SODA error codes (`no-such-column`, `query.soql`, `query.unknown`) to `soql_error` — other 400 error codes (e.g. `query.compiler.malformed`) fall through to `httpErrorFromResponse`, which discards the SODA message entirely.

**Actual response (input: `where: "INVALID SOQL $$% @#$"`):**
```json
{
  "isError": true,
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Error: Socrata returned HTTP 400 Bad Request." }],
  "structuredContent": {
    "error": {
      "code": -32602,
      "message": "Socrata returned HTTP 400 Bad Request.",
      "data": {
        "url": "https://data.seattle.gov/resource/...",
        "status": 400,
        "statusText": "Bad Request"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

No `reason`, no recovery hint, no upstream SODA message about what was wrong with the query.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Call `socrata_query_dataset` with a valid dataset ID and an invalid `where` clause (e.g. `"INVALID SOQL"` or a non-existent column name).
2. Observe a generic 400 error with no actionable detail.

### Expected behavior

When Socrata returns any 400 with a structured SODA error body, the error should:
- Propagate the upstream `message` field (e.g. "Unknown column `xyz`")
- Set `reason: 'soql_error'` so the declared contract entry fires
- Include the recovery hint: "Check column names with `socrata_get_dataset`. Text columns need single-quoted strings..."

### Root cause

In `socrata-service.ts` `fetchJson`, the SODA code matching only covers three code strings. Any other 400 (including `query.compiler.malformed` from malformed WHERE syntax) falls through to `httpErrorFromResponse`, which only has `status`/`statusText` and discards the already-parsed `sodaErr.message`.

Fix: when `sodaErr` is truthy and status is 400 (and not already matched by the narrow code check), throw `validationError(...)` with `reason: 'soql_error'` and the upstream `sodaErr.message` as the message body. This ensures all 400s with a SODA body hit the contract entry.

### Verified against current source (2026-07-04)

Confirmed live against `data.cityofchicago.org`. Socrata uses two different key names for the SODA error code depending on which subsystem raised the error:

| Error family | Live example | Code key |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Query coordinator (`no-such-column`) | `{"message":"...","errorCode":"query.soql.no-such-column","data":{...}}` | `errorCode` |
| SoQL compiler (malformed syntax) | `{"code":"query.compiler.malformed","error":true,"message":"...","data":{...}}` | `code` |

`fetchJson` in `socrata-service.ts` gates SODA-error detection on `'code' in parsed && 'message' in parsed`. A body using `errorCode` fails this check and falls through to the generic `httpErrorFromResponse` path — exactly the regression. Fix: accept either key.

Also verified: even for the family that IS detected today, the declared `soql_error` recovery hint never reaches the client. `query-dataset.tool.ts`'s catch block only re-throws via `ctx.fail`/`ctx.recoveryFor` for `reason === 'not_found'`; `soql_error` and `rate_limited` fall through unchanged, so `data.recovery.hint` is never populated for them — required by this issue's own "Expected behavior" section above.

### Touchpoints

- `src/services/socrata/types.ts` — widen `SodaError` to accept `errorCode` as an alternative to `code` (`message` stays required).
- `src/services/socrata/socrata-service.ts` — `fetchJson`: accept `errorCode` alongside `code` in the shape guard; read `sodaErr.code ?? sodaErr.errorCode ?? ''` wherever the code value is used.
- `src/mcp-server/tools/definitions/query-dataset.tool.ts` — catch block: add `soql_error` (and `rate_limited`) alongside the existing `not_found` branch so `ctx.recoveryFor(reason)` actually attaches the declared recovery hint.
- Tests: no service-level test file exists yet (`tests/services/`) — all current coverage mocks `getSocrataService()` and never exercises `fetchJson`'s error-shape detection. Add one covering both the `errorCode` and `code` families via a mocked `global.fetch`, plus a `tests/tools/query-dataset.tool.test.ts` case asserting the recovery hint reaches the wire for a service-thrown `soql_error`.

items.title: Authorization issue with Google Maps MCP Server
items.body:
**Describe the bug**
I encountered an authorization issue when attempting to use `Google Maps MCP`, despite all pre-requisites had been in place. The error I received was: This API project is not authorized to use this API.

Upon investigation, it appears that Google Maps MCP Server is pointing to a legacy Places API endpoint, which my newly created API key is not able to authorize against.

Google provides two versions of the Places API:
1. **Legacy Places API**: Uses endpoints like `https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/place/*`
2. **Places API (New) / V1**: Uses endpoints like `https://places.googleapis.com/v1/*`

I did a separate test to verify that my API key works correctly with the Places API (New) V1 endpoints but fails with the legacy endpoints. This suggests that the Google Maps MCP Server needs to be updated to use the newer API endpoints.


**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

**Complete pre-requisites**
1. Create a new Google Cloud Project and enable billing, or ensure an existing Google Cloud Project has billing enabled.
2. Enable the Places API (New) / V1 in the Google Cloud Console
3. Create a new API key with access to Places API

**Repro steps**
1. Add Google Maps MCP Server to Claude Desktop configuration json. Add your API key as well.
2. Restart Claude Desktop.
3. Chat with Claude and ask a question like `10 best coffee places in Seattle`
4. Claude responds with they are experiencing an issue `Place search failed: This API project is not authorized to use this API.`

**Expected behavior**
Claude shouldn't have an authorization issue with the prompt. The Google Maps MCP Server should work with API keys that are authorized for the Places API (New) / V1, which is the current version of the API.

Question: Why start a new session on each tool call in MultiServerMCPClient? (Causes issues with stateful MCP servers in stdio mode)
items.body:
Thank you for you guys great work on this project!

I’m reaching out with a question regarding the current behavior of the MultiServerMCPClient class — specifically, why a new session is started on every tool call.

This design causes issues when working with stateful MCP servers, such as [NightTrek/Software-planning-mcp](https://github.com/NightTrek/Software-planning-mcp), which rely on session persistence across multiple tool calls. Since each tool call creates a new session, any state saved in previous calls is lost, leading to errors.

This becomes particularly problematic in stdio mode, where tools are expected to maintain context throughout the session. With a fresh session each time, it becomes impossible to carry forward any meaningful planning or interaction state.

Could you please clarify the reasoning behind this behavior? Was it designed this way to support only stateless scenarios, or might there be a way to support persistent sessions for cases like this?

Looking forward to your thoughts!

items.title: [BUG] MCP session 404 in multi worker production environment
items.body:
# Issue: `404 session not found` error due to session not shared across instances behind load balancer

Hi,

I've implemented an MCP server and during local testing with the `mcp_use` client in `SSE` configuration, everything works as expected.

However, after deploying the code to production, I started encountering a `404 session not found` error.

Upon inspecting the logs, I realized that the root cause is that the `session` is being created on one instance, but since the application is running behind a load balancer, requests are distributed across different instances/pods. This causes the session lookup to fail when subsequent requests hit a different instance than the one where the session was initially created.

Is there any recommended way to persist or share session state across instances, or any guidance for running MCP server behind a load balancer in a multi-instance environment?

Thanks!

items.title: [BUG] [BUG] Claude Desktop MCP tools failing with "Required" parameter error
items.body:
# [BUG] Claude Desktop MCP tools failing with parameter validation error - July 23, 2025

## Bug Description
Claude Desktop MCP tools suddenly stopped working on July 23, 2025. All MCP tools are failing with parameter validation errors when called by Claude Desktop, despite the MCP servers themselves functioning correctly.

## Environment
- **Date**: July 23, 2025
- **Platform**: Multiple computers affected (confirming this is not a local configuration issue)
- **Claude Desktop Version**: [Please check your version]
- **Operating System**: [Please specify your OS]

## Expected Behavior
MCP tools should receive proper parameters when called by Claude Desktop and execute successfully as they did until July 22, 2025.

## Actual Behavior
- Claude Desktop calls MCP tools without required parameters
- All tool calls result in validation errors
- Error indicates `"expected": "object", "received": "undefined"`
- MCP servers themselves are working (connection established, communication functional)

## Reproduction Steps
1. Have any MCP server configured and running (e.g., filesystem)
2. Try to use any MCP tool through Claude Desktop interface
3. Observe the parameter validation error in MCP logs

## Error Logs
```
2025-07-23T04:39:51.994Z [filesystem] [info] Message from client: {"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_directory"},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":16} { metadata: undefined }
2025-07-23T04:39:51.995Z [filesystem] [info] Message from server: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":16,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: Invalid arguments for list_directory: [\n  {\n    \"code\": \"invalid_type\",\n    \"expected\": \"object\",\n    \"received\": \"undefined\",\n    \"path\": [],\n    \"message\": \"Required\"\n  }\n]"}],"isError":true}} { metadata: undefined }
```

## Analysis
1. **MCP Server Status**: ✅ Working correctly (connection established, responds to calls)
2. **Client-Server Communication**: ✅ Working (messages are being exchanged)
3. **Parameter Passing**: ❌ **Claude Desktop is not passing required parameters to MCP tools**

## Additional Context
- **Timeline**: Worked perfectly until July 22, 2025, suddenly broke on July 23, 2025
- **Scope**: Multiple users on different computers experiencing the same issue simultaneously
- **Impact**: All MCP functionality is currently broken in Claude Desktop
- **Workaround**: None available - this appears to be an internal Claude Desktop issue

## Root Cause Assessment
This appears to be a regression introduced in Claude Desktop's MCP tool calling mechanism, where the application is no longer properly packaging tool parameters before sending them to MCP servers.

## Priority
**High** - This completely breaks MCP functionality for all users, which is a core feature of Claude Desktop.

---

**Note**: This issue appears to coincide with reported Claude service instabilities on July 23, 2025, suggesting this may be related to a recent update or backend change.

items.title: Proposal: add a simpler version of AddTool that drops request and response

labels.name: needs community feedback
labels.description: More input from users needed to inform a decision

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
Currently, `mcp.AddTool` takes a `ToolHandlerFor[In, Out]`, which is defined as 
```
func(context.Context, *CallToolRequest, In) (*CallToolResult, Out, error)
```
As argued on #386, the request and result are seldom used and confusing. In particular, it is unclear whether to use the StructuredOutput and IsError fields of CallToolResult, or to return results via the second and third return values.

The proposal is to change AddTool to take a handler with signature
```
func(context.Context, In) (Out, error)
```
That will satisfy the majority of tool authors and remove the confusion.

items.title: Official Agent Suggestions Thread
items.body:
(Started from discussions in #344)
## Official 'suggest an agent' thread for Huginn!!

**Have a cool idea for an agent that you want to see implemented?**
- Firstly, please check to see if the agent is already on the list.
- Also have a quick look through the [Issues](https://github.com/cantino/huginn/issues/) to make sure it's not already being worked on.
- Comment on this thread and we will add it to the list below!
- If the agent is already on this list but you still want to throw extra support behind it, feel free to comment with your +1

**Want to work on one of the agents on the list?**
- Create a new issue/pull request to discuss it and reference this issue so we can reference it on the list below and mark it as being in progress.
- If there is already an issue reference and it's closed, tag one of us to reopen the issue for you.
## Agent Suggestions

(Note: This list should be maintained in alphabetical order, ticked items mean in progress/actively being worked on, ticked items should be moved to 'in progress' list)
### In Progress
- [x] Delayed Reaction Agent (#174, #197?)
- [x] Event Mixer Agent (#262)
- [x] @KenYN's Time Gateway Agent (#351)
- [x] Real RSS Agent (#11, #203)
### Backlog
- [x] AfterShip Agent (#295)
- [ ] AgentCreatorAgent([#459](https://github.com/cantino/huginn/pull/459#discussion_r16628653))
- [ ] AgentDiagnosticAgent([#459](https://github.com/cantino/huginn/pull/459#discussion_r16628653))
- [ ] App.net support (incl. for Broadcasts and other Channels)
- [ ] Bitcoin Agent - send and receive Bitcoin payments
- [ ] Bitcoin Spending Agent (#183)
- [ ] Boxcar support for sending push notification messages to iOS devices
- [x] CalendarAgent ([#459](https://github.com/cantino/huginn/pull/459#issuecomment-53028041))
- [ ] CalendarOutputAgent (like DataOutputAgent; I would probably write one - @knu)
- [ ] Clipper Agent (#66)
- [ ] DeviantArt Agent (#289)
- [x] Dropbox Agent (#321)
- [ ] Evernote Agent (#320)
- [ ] Fancy Hands Agent (#319)
- [ ] Feedly support (get marked for later)
- [ ] Geofencing Agent (#5)
- [ ] GitHub agent see https://github.com/peter-murach/github
- [ ] Gmail Agent (#10)
- [x] Google Calendar Agent (#344)
- [ ] Google Diff Match Patch support http://code.google.com/p/google-diff-match-patch/
- [ ] Google Search results (changes in SERP for specified keyword and/or specified url)
- [ ] Google Spreadsheets
- [ ] Hubot Agent (#352)
- [ ] IFTTT -> Huginn Bridge Agent (#331)
- [ ] IRC Agent (#113)
- [ ] A Jabber Agent that listens for incoming messages and spits them out as Events
- [ ] Naive Bayes Agent - classify events based on training data
- [ ] MailFetching Agent (#129)
- [ ] Mqtt subscriber/publisher (see http://mqtt.org)
- [ ] Monitoring 'acceleration/deceleration' of values (#178)
- [ ] PagerDuty - trigger [PagerDuty](http://developer.pagerduty.com/documentation/integration/events) incidents based on events, _or_ take different actions based on incoming PagerDuty incidents.
- [ ] Pocket support ( put something into read queue)
- [ ] Readability support ( put something into read later)
- [ ] Reddit Agent (#16)
- [ ] RescueTime support (detect/report productivity or lack thereof)
- [ ] Trakt.tv Agent http://trakt.tv/api-docs
- [ ] Tumblr Agent (#290)
- [x] Website status monitoring (alert when website is down)
- [ ] Websockets Agent (#192)
- [ ] Whois tracking (detect changes in whois details for a domain)
- [ ] WSDL-defined web-service Agent
- [ ] [Zinc.io](http://www.zinc.io) Agent
### Done
- [x] CommanderAgent (AgentRunnerAgent [#459](https://github.com/cantino/huginn/pull/459#issuecomment-53028041) -> #570)
- [x] Pushover support (#233)
### Similar services to Huginn (for inspiration)

items.title: BearerTokenValidator:validateAuthorization seems to incorrectly use the audience claim.
items.body:
// Return the request with additional attributes
            return $request
                ->withAttribute('oauth_access_token_id', $token->getClaim('jti'))
                ->withAttribute('oauth_client_id', $token->getClaim('aud'))
                ->withAttribute('oauth_user_id', $token->getClaim('sub'))
                ->withAttribute('oauth_scopes', $token->getClaim('scopes'));

The appears to expect the client identifier as audience which seems to conflict with the bearer spec here.  It's possible I am misunderstanding this spec as it is possible to reject a token based on the relationship between client_id and authorization server but that is not clear to me.

https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-ietf-oauth-jwt-bearer-12#section-3

3.   The JWT MUST contain an "aud" (audience) claim containing a
        value that identifies the authorization server as an intended
        audience.  The token endpoint URL of the authorization server
        MAY be used as a value for an "aud" element to identify the
        authorization server as an intended audience of the JWT.  The
        Authorization Server MUST reject any JWT that does not contain
        its own identity as the intended audience In the absence of an
        application profile specifying otherwise, compliant applications
        MUST compare the audience values using the Simple String
        Comparison method defined in Section 6.2.1 of RFC 3986
        [RFC3986].  As noted in Section 5, the precise strings to be
        used as the audience for a given Authorization Server must be
        configured out-of-band by the Authorization Server and the
        Issuer of the JWT.

items.title: Rationalize namespaced vs. cluster scoped MCP resources

milestone.title: Nebulous Future
milestone.description: Issues unlikely to get addressed in the near term

items.body:
We use the same type_url for namespace and cluster scoped MCP resources (e.g. see [Policy vs. MeshPolicy](https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/feae02be949a5958567616485655efb9f279851b/galley/tools/gen-meta/metadata.yaml#L68-L81)). MCP clients cannot differentiate between the two scopes and, as a result, policy is misapplied. 

For networking APIs, namespace scoped resources provide some convenience w/k8s short names. Namespace based ACL'ing is still [WIP](http://bit.ly/2nGO5cx).

For authentication APIs, Policy can be applied to all services/workloads in a namespace or for _all_ services/workloads (i.e. mesh scoped). 

For Mixer Policy APIs, scope is resolved at runtime per request against the attribute match expression. Namespace'd configuration that should not apply to a particular request is silently ignored at runtime.

A few options to consider:

1) Create new protobuf types for mesh scoped resources,  e.g. `type.googleapis.com/istio.authentication.v1alpha1.MeshPolicy`
2) Resuse the existing protobuf types and encode scope as additional metadata in the type_url, e.g. `type.googleapis.com/istio.authentication.v1alpha1.MeshPolicy?scope=mesh`
3) Fully normalize resource scope outside Istio runtime components (Pilot / Mixer).

(1) and (2) requires components to resolve mesh vs. namespace/service/workload scope. That already do this today. (3) requires moving some (all?) scope resolution into Galley (or equiv.).


- Platform specific service name resolution for networking APIs is fairly straightforward, assuming knowledge of service topology is not required, e.g. short name `foo` in namespace `bar` resolves to `foo.bar.svc.cluster.local`. 
- Workload resolution is TBD and currently assumes fixed mapping of service-to-workload.
- Namespace resolution requires complete knowledge of services / workloads in each namespace. Istio APIs that select targets by namespace including AuthenticationPolicy and possibly Mixer rules.

Fully resolving scope per service/workload at config ingestion time requires additional component-level design work. For example, Pilot resolves mesh and namespace scoped resources on-demand because proxy's identity includes scope (name/namespace). The default mesh authentication policy is unconditionally applied to _any_ workload if no lesser scoped policy exists. Pilot _doesn't_ pre-resolve per workload/service configuration.

cc @geeknoid @ozevren @liminw @andraxylia
